answer: Registration requires every agent to lock a stake and sign with a unique key. A public randomness beacon, the lantern, periodically selects identities that must attest to past work. A missed attestation slashes that stake, and a ripple of forfeiture spreads to any alias sharing funding or hardware fingerprints. Each fake identity therefore needs its own bond: a Sybil farm of N agents must post N stakes and risks losing all of them in one audit, so the whole wharf of colluding agents sinks together. Cost grows linearly with identity count, making the attack unprofitable.
